A slice that folded them into one anchor would have shipped a block refusing a Poison the card does not refuse. **AND THE COUNT WAS A FLOOR RATHER THAN A TOTAL**: §D134's census was `LIKE '%Flip a coin. the pipeline still RUNS (Weakness is computed and reported) and the block nulls the RESULT, so it SUPERSEDES rather than stacks. **IN, effects half (the WIDER reading only):** §12 Special Conditions on the body, the §11 retreat rider, an Energy discarded off it, the destination half of a counter MOVE, and — the sharpest — **damage COUNTERS PUT on it**, because this engine has ruled since D138/D139 that a placement is not attack damage (it skips Weakness, Resistance and every reduction passive), so it falls **entirely** on the effects side and a **NARROW block does not stop it**. **OUT:** anything an attack does to a **different** Pokémon (one Spread Shot declaration is prevented on the shielded Active and lands 20 on every benched body); anything done to the **PLAYER** rather than to a Pokémon (a mill, a hand disruption); the attacker's own recoil and the §9 counterattack (done to the ATTACKER); and **everything that is not an ATTACK** — a Trainer, an activated or triggered Ability, a §13 Checkup tick. **⚠️ THE STATE IS A TURN STAMP, AND THE REASON IS NOT D124's — THIS IS THE HEADLINE.** D124 chose a stamp to avoid a boundary clear a future slice could forget; here **the boundary clear that already exists is actively WRONG**. D112's `retreatBlocked` reuses §13.4's paralysis clock (cleared in `runCheckup` for `endedSeat`) and that works because the retreat block sits on the **DEFENDER's** body. **This one sits on the INSTALLER's OWN**, so the very first Checkup after the attack has `endedSeat` = the holder's seat and the same clear **lifts the block a full turn EARLY, before its window has opened at all** — two shapes that look identical in a doc and are mirror images in the code. `InPlayPokemon.attackBlock: { turn: number; effects: boolean } | null` therefore stamps **`state.turn + 1`** (declaring an attack ENDS the turn per §5.3, so the next turn is the opponent's *by construction* — no seat is stored and none is needed) and expires **by arithmetic**, with nothing anywhere to clear it and the stale stamp deliberately left sitting on the card. **Measured: reusing D112's clock fails 12 tests; stamping the installing turn instead of the next one fails the same 12.** **⚠️ "EFFECTS OF ATTACKS" IS A PROVENANCE THE TARGET CANNOT ANSWER, SO IT RIDES `EffectContext.invokedBy?: "attack"` — AND THIS REFINES D139 RATHER THAN REVERSING IT.** D139 explicitly declined a context field and put the provenance on the OP (`damageActive`/`damageChosen` still carry `source`, and still should) because a **LOG LABEL** is a property of the row an op emits. What rides on the CONTEXT is a **RULE that SIX ops must answer identically**, and the only site that knows the answer is the one that started the program: written per op it would be one fact in six places with six chances to go stale. D139's second objection — that `ctx` is serialized into every park — is exactly what makes it right here: an attack effect that PARKS and resolves three actions later is still an attack's effect, and an old continuation lacking the field reads as "not an attack", which is byte-identically the pre-slice behaviour. **The two provenances are PINNED TO AGREE** on every producer in the pool. Without the check Crushing Hammer and Boss's Orders stop working inside the window; the sharpest witness is **Trevenant's between-turns Ability reaching the SAME `damageActive` op an attack reaches**, firing at the Checkup that ends the window turn where `state.turn` is still the block's own number and only `invokedBy` can save it. **⚠️ `effects` IS A FIELD — D131's widen-don't-add rule applied and PASSING (the D139 case, not D138's)**: same install site, holder, stamp, event, expiry and three early clears, and the suite asserts the two derived programs are **byte-identical once the one field is stripped**. OPTIONAL, with the polarity deliberate (D135's `zone` from the other end): the printed words WIDEN the block, so a producer that forgets it blocks **LESS** rather than more. **NOT widened to a `damage` flag**, with the warranting condition written down — Palafin `sv03-145`'s effects-WITHOUT-damage reading, ONE printing on a different sentence. **⚠️ THE EARLY CLEARS ARE §10's, AND WHICH ONE IS REACHABLE IS INVERTED FROM D112's**: the **EVOLVE** clear is **unreachable by construction** (installing ends the turn, the window is the opponent's, nobody evolves on someone else's turn) and is written anyway with a surgery pinning the rule, while the **SWITCH** clear is reachable in the sharpest possible way — a **Boss's Orders played INSIDE the window** drags the shielded body off the spot and the protection goes with it, pinned by a following Spread Shot landing **20 on the very body that was immune a moment earlier**. Both stay SILENT (the `POKEMON_SWITCHED`/`POKEMON_EVOLVED` row tells the story — D112's own call). **⚠️ THE ONLY WAY TO KNOCK OUT A SHIELDED POKÉMON is a counter PUT through the NARROW reading** — the wide one refuses the placement and the damage half refuses every hit — driven end to end (`COUNTERS_PLACED` < `KNOCKED_OUT` < `PRIZES_OWED` to the attacker). **⚠️ TWO NEW EVENTS, AND THE VOICE IS THE MIRROR OF D141's**: `ATTACK_BLOCK_APPLIED { seat, uid, effects }` renders in the **ACTIVE** voice — `seat` owns the shielded Pokémon **and** that Pokémon is the ACTOR's own, where `RETREAT_BLOCKED`'s seat owns the victim and D141's causer is the other player — with deliberately **no `…_ENDED` twin** (a stamp expires with nothing to announce, and manufacturing a row would reintroduce the per-turn scan the stamp exists to avoid); `ATTACK_EFFECT_PREVENTED { seat, uid }` fires **once per refused op**, because a silently-skipped attack clause reads exactly like a bug. The damage half needs no event — `DAMAGE_DEALT.prevented` has named that FACT since Safeguard (0.58.0). **⚠️ `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 3 → 4, AND IT IS D124's CASE RATHER THAN D140's**: no `EffectOp` moved at all; what moved is a **new REQUIRED field on `InPlayPokemon`**, so every Pokémon in play in an old record lacks it — and it would read back **BENIGNLY** (`undefined.turn` is never `state.turn`, and no such block could have been installed by a deploy with no op to install one), which is exactly the soft landing that constant exists to refuse. `EffectContext.invokedBy` is OPTIONAL and therefore a WIDENING (D125's distinction), asked about explicitly rather than folded in. **⚠️ THE GUARD IS SWEPT, NOT LISTED (D140's move)**: the suite DISCOVERS every op kind any attack in `FIXTURE_POOL` can produce — walking `coinFlipGate` bodies, since this whole family hides inside one — and asserts the §11 classification is **TOTAL over the discovered set in BOTH directions**, so a slice that teaches the deriver a new op fails there until it has said which side of the reading that op falls on. **Cost: 1 op member + impl, 1 state field + type, 1 `continuous.ts` reader (`attackBlockOf`), 2 events, 2 log arms, 2 regexes, 2 deriver arms, 1 `EffectContext` field, 6 guarded effect sites, 4 damage sites, 3 early clears, `preventBlock.test.ts` (32 tests) on its own `PREVENT_BLOCK_DECK`, 2 fixtures (Scyther `sv03-004` — the wide reading with a printed 10, a D125 tail board; **⚠️ AND THE STANDING DESIGN RULE GAINS ITS EIGHTH PAYOUT AND A NEW SECOND HALF: THE
UNIT OF SHARING IS DECIDED BY THE READ SITE — AND THE UNIT OF *STORAGE* IS DECIDED BY
THE WRITE SITES.**

D155 refused to merge `boostedAttack` into `lockedAttack` because the consumers
disagree; D157 reused `lockedAttack` unchanged because they agree; D158 split
`damageAttackerOnKo` from `damageAttacker` because they MUTUALLY REFUSE; D159 refused
one shared prevention record on three axes; D161 split two after-W/R reductions; D163
answered both ways in one slice; D164 made `PRIZE_REDUCED` a SIBLING of Glimmora's
guard on three axes. **D165 is the eighth and it is the one that adds a question
nobody had been asking.** Every decision above is about whether two facts may share a
CONSUMER. D157's was too — and it was right about that and wrong anyway, because
sharing a consumer and sharing a SLOT are different questions and it answered only the
first. **Before you reuse a stamped field, count its WRITERS and ask whether any two
of them can stamp the same turn.** A reader count cannot tell you.

⚠️ **D166 ADDS NO NINTH PAYOUT — IT IS NOT A SHARING DECISION — BUT IT ADDS A
COROLLARY THAT BELONGS HERE.** Once a slot becomes a COLLECTION, it acquires a
**garbage rule** beside its merge rule, and **the garbage rule has the merge rule's
failure mode**: `addLockedAttack` prunes `lock.turn >= now`, and every one of the five
mutants that survived D165's pass was that `>=` — each of them deleting a bar that is
still biting, which is bit-for-bit the defect the list was introduced to fix, one line
further down. **When you turn a slot into a list, mutate the rule that EMPTIES it as
hard as the rule that FILLS it.**

**⚠️ AND THE COROLLARY, WHICH IS WHERE THE `attackBlock` UNION FINALLY MOVED.** Four
decisions (§D147, §D152, §D154, §D157) forecast a trigger for a collection over the
durated riders and four declined it, all on the same ground: *no read site
ENUMERATES; every reader knows which rider it wants before it looks.* **That was a
claim about rider KINDS, it is still true, and it is not the only way a collection is
earned.** D165's field became a list because ONE kind acquired a MULTIPLICITY the read
sites must enumerate. **The union is still declined — nothing dispatches, because
every entry means one thing — but "no site enumerates" is now a claim that has to be
re-checked against MULTIPLICITY as well as against KIND.**

⚠️ **D167 IS THE NINTH PAYOUT, AND IT IS THE FIRST ONE THAT PAID OUT YEARS AFTER THE
DECISION: THE AXIS YOU SHARE AN INTERFACE ALONG DECIDES WHAT A LATER ARRIVAL COSTS.**
The damage-scaling family is **one `{per, count}` interface and one count evaluator,
split into THREE READERS BY FOLD** — `+` keeps the printed base and adds, `×` drops it,
`−` keeps it and subtracts — rather than split by COUNT SOURCE. Until D167 **every fold
happened to own a disjoint set of sources**, so the two partitions were
indistinguishable and it would have been easy to read the accident as the design.
D167's printing put `damageCountersOnSelf` under **all three readers at once, told apart
by a single word**, and the bill for that third arrival was **one regex and one `if`** —
no new source, evaluator arm, reader, fold or branch in `attack.ts`, because every
consumer was already written against the READER rather than against the `count` member.
**Compare D163, which paid for a whole third reader because its FOLD was new.** The
transferable rule: **when a family shares an interface, ask which axis the SPLIT is on,
and price a new printing by whether it is new ALONG THAT AXIS.** *"Is this a new count
source, or a new fold?"* is a question with an order-of-magnitude answer, and it is the
same question in a different coat as D155's *"do the CONSUMERS agree?"*.

⚠️ **D168 IS THE TENTH PAYOUT, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THE ANSWER WAS "TWO MEMBERS"
RATHER THAN "ONE MEMBER WITH A FIELD".** `damageCountersOnSelf` and
`damageCountersOnOpponentActive` tally the **identical resource** —
`InPlayPokemon.damage ÷ 10` — off two different bodies, which is exactly the shape that
looks like it wants one member plus a `side: "self" | "opponent"` discriminator. It was
priced and REFUSED at the read site, as the rule says: **every consumer of the union
dispatches on `kind` and nothing else**, so a `side` would have to be read by
`scaledAttackDamage` anyway (no line saved) and the **three members that have no side at
all would then carry a field they must ignore** (a line spent). D163 refused a
`direction` discriminator on the same ground one axis over. **When "one member with a
flag" and "two members" cost the read site the same, the members win — the flag is a lie
told to every member that has no opinion about it.** And because the two members MIRROR
each other, the slice owes the mirror's own defect a witness: a board with **9 counters
on the attacker and 3 on the defender** (self scores 270, a sum 360, the right answer
**90**) and **both census sweeps asserted side by side**, so a reader that started
answering both would collapse two lists into one.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D168): AN ORDERING CLAIM NEEDS A WITNESS THAT DOES NOT
COMMUTE — AND A SUBTRACTIVE TERM CAN NEVER BE ONE.** D168 had to prove its fold lands
BEFORE Weakness/Resistance, and the obvious board was the wrong board: Espeon's **−30
Fighting Resistance** is a SUBTRACTION, and subtraction **commutes** with the fold's
addition, so `(100 + 30) − 30` and `(100 − 30) + 30` are both 100 and **the two
placements are indistinguishable there**. A suite written on that board would have
"passed" while asserting nothing about the order. **Only a MULTIPLY W/R separates the
placements**, so the order is driven on Tyranitar ex `sv03-066` (340 HP, ×2 Fighting):
`(100 + 60) × 2 = 320` lands a body already carrying 20 on **exactly 340 — a KO** —
where the reversed `100 × 2 + 60 = 260` leaves it alive with 60 HP, so **two observables
move together**. The generalisation is not about damage at all: **before you claim step A
happens before step B, check that your board's B is not an operation that COMMUTES with
A.** The commuting board is still worth keeping for what it CAN show (here: the scaled
total carrying a defender past a subtractive term it survived a moment earlier) — **but
say in the test that it is not the order witness**, or the next reader will think it is.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D168): A GENERATED FILE MUST BE REGENERATED, NEVER
TEXT-MERGED, WHEN TWO SLICES TOUCH IT.** D167 and D168 ran in **parallel worktrees** and
both regenerated `catalogManifest.ts` **independently from the same 209-row base**,
producing **211** and **212**. The true merged figure is **214**, and **no textual
resolution of the two diffs would have produced it** — a three-way merge of a generated
file resolves *cleanly* and is still wrong, because the file is a **FUNCTION of inputs
neither side had whole**. The manifest was regenerated after the merge and D168's own
changelog line corrected from *"209 → 212"* to **"211 → 214"**. Two consequences: **(1)
when two branches touch a generated file, the merge is a RE-RUN of the generator, not a
resolution of the text** — and `bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts --check` is the thing
that tells you; **(2) any number a worktree handoff quotes for a generated file was
measured against a base that no longer exists**, so re-derive it, exactly as the
`FIXTURE_POOL` size has had to be re-derived three handoffs running.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D169): A SHARED SEAM'S OPENING GUARD CAN BELONG TO ONLY ONE
OF ITS TERMS, AND THE SECOND TERM INHERITS IT INVISIBLY.** `effectiveAttackCost` opened
`if (top === undefined || !isBasicPokemon(top)) return cost;`. That Basic test is
**League HQ's printed *"each BASIC Pokémon in play"* and nothing else** — but it sat
where a reader sees the FUNCTION's precondition, and neither the type, the name nor any
existing test says which term owns it. **Seismitoad is a Stage 2**, so keeping it would
have silently switched the new aura off against every Stage 1/2 Active it aims at, on
the one card whose own stage guarantees the case comes up. It is now a per-TERM gate
(`stadiumRetreatDelta` made exactly this move when the first stage-agnostic aura reached
the retreat seam — **the second time a Stadium's stage clause has been mistaken for a
seam's, both times exposed by a cross-board Ability**), and restoring it is the mutant
that kills **4** tests. **When you widen a function that already serves one printing,
read its EARLY RETURNS as the OLD term's preconditions rather than as the function's** —
and note that **neither the recon pass nor the slice brief found this**, which is what
makes it a standing warning rather than a slice note: it is invisible to anyone reading
the seam from the outside.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D169): A MUTANT MUST BE THE MISTAKE SOMEONE WOULD ACTUALLY
MAKE.** D169's sixth mutant — dropping the surcharge's SOURCE Active clause — was first
written as `foes.active ?? foes.bench[0]`, **which never reaches the bench on a board
that has an Active**, and it SURVIVED. It was not a weak test; it was not a mutation.
Re-written as the *realistic* wrong implementation — `opposingRetreatSurcharge`'s
Active+Bench source loop, which is exactly the sibling scan a future author would copy —
it was caught at once. **A mutation that no author would write proves nothing about the
suite. Write the mutant as the NEIGHBOURING SCAN'S REAL CODE**, and when one survives,
ask first whether it was a plausible implementation before concluding the suite is
thin. (Record first-round survivors either way — D166's rule: a pass's own report is
the one number nothing in the repo can contradict.)

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D170) — THE CONVERSE OF D168's ORDERING RULE: WHERE A FOLD
HAS ONE TERM, THE ORDERING QUESTION DOES NOT ARISE, AND A TEST THAT CLAIMS TO WITNESS IT
IS TESTING NOTHING. PIN THE ABSENCE.** D170 was dispatched to drive a non-commuting W/R
order witness, on D168's warning above. **No such witness can exist in that family.** The
`×` fold **drops the printed base**, so the fold has exactly one term and

```
(0 + 60) × 2  =  0 × 2 + 60 × 2  =  120
```

agree **by DISTRIBUTION**, not by luck and not by a badly chosen board — where the
additive fold's `(100 + 60) × 2 ≠ 100 × 2 + 60` is exactly why D168 *could* drive an
order. D168's rule says an ordering claim needs a witness that does not commute; **the
other half is that some families cannot produce one at all**, and the honest move there
is an **assertion that says so** rather than a board that "looks like" an order test and
passes while asserting nothing. D170's ×2 board is therefore relabelled as what it
really witnesses — the **base drop surviving a multiply** (120 against a leaked
`(10 + 60) × 2 = 140`) — and **the absence is pinned as its own case**. Generally:
**before you write an ordering test, count the TERMS. One term means there is no order
to witness; say so in the suite, and do not let a passing board imply otherwise.**

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D170) — AND IT IS ABOUT THIS PAGE ITSELF: THE REMAINDER
LIST'S OWN COSTING METHOD HAS NOW BEEN SHORT BY THE SAME TWO EDITS TWICE.** D168 and
D170 both inherited *"one regex + one evaluator arm"* from the item below, and **both
were short by exactly the same pair — the READER ARM and the UNION MEMBER.** Two slices
in a row, on the same page, in the same way, is **a property of the method rather than a
slip about either card**: *the list prices the SENTENCE and the FOLD, and forgets that a
new SOURCE is three edits, not one.* **A new `DamageCountSource` is FOUR edits (regex +
reader arm + union member + evaluator arm); a new FOLD on an old source is TWO.** So:
**read any future "one regex + one evaluator arm" costing on this page as AT LEAST FOUR
EDITS until it has been re-derived against the file.** This sits beside the eleventh
dangerous claim (*a pricing's own list of edits*) and is its sharpest instance —
the same enumeration was wrong the same way twice, and nothing in the repo objected
either time.

⚠️ **PROMOTED AT D171 FROM AN OBSERVATION TO A CHECKLIST ITEM — D169's ONE-TERM-GUARD
WARNING HAS NOW RECURRED ONE SLICE LATER, WHICH MAKES IT LOAD-BEARING.** D169 found
`effectiveAttackCost` opening with a `!isBasicPokemon` early return that belonged to
League HQ's printed *"each BASIC Pokémon in play"* and to nothing else. **D171 found the
same shape one slice later, in a different file, on a different seam**: `attachTool`'s
simulation gate was `programFor(id)?.passive !== undefined`, which is *"is this Tool
simulated"* answered for the Tools that happened to exist — every authored Tool up to
Vengeful Punch expressed its sentence as continuous NUMBERS, so *"has a passive"* and
*"is simulated"* were the same predicate **by accident**. Exp. Share has a `triggered`
program and **no passive**, so the unwidened gate would have **refused to attach a card
the engine fully simulates**, with the message *"not simulated yet"*. **A warning that
recurs one slice after it is written is not an anecdote.** So it is now a step rather
than a story: **WHEN YOU WIDEN A SEAM THAT ALREADY SERVES ONE PRINTING, ENUMERATE ITS
EARLY RETURNS AND ASK, OF EACH ONE, WHICH TERM IT BELONGS TO.** Neither type, name nor
existing test will tell you — both sightings were invisible to a recon pass and to the
slice brief, and both were found only by opening the function.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D171) — THE SECOND HALF OF D169's MUTATION RULE: A MUTANT
THAT COPIES A SIBLING'S REAL CODE NEEDS A BOARD THE SIBLING NEVER HAS.** D169 established
that a mutant must be *the mistake someone would actually make*. D171's `koToolTrigger`
seed sits one block from `damagedTrigger`'s, which seeds inside the damage block on
`dealt > 0` — so *"seed on `dealt > 0`"* is the realistic wrong implementation, written
as the neighbour's literal text, and **it SURVIVED the first pass**. Not because the
suite was thin, but because **every board in it dealt main damage — which is exactly the
board the sibling is designed for.** It was killed only after **Mimikyu `sv02-097` "Ghost
Eye"** was found: {P}{C}, **no printed `damage` field** (so the §8.5 pipeline is skipped
whole) and a lethal EFFECT PROGRAM (7 damage counters). **The printed condition is the
KNOCK OUT, not the HIT.** Generally: **when your mutant IS a sibling's real code, the
board that kills it is by construction absent from the sibling's own coverage — go find
the case where the two siblings disagree before concluding the mutant is unkillable.**

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D171) — A ROW A CENSUS CANNOT SEE SHOULD BE PINNED IN CODE,
NOT RE-NOTED IN PROSE EACH TIME.** **Corviknight `sv02-148` "Accelerate"** prints
*"Knocked Out by damage from **THIS** attack"*, so the KO-antecedent census pattern
(*"from an attack"*) has been blind to it since D158. **Three separate passes have now
rediscovered it**, each writing it into a handoff, and none of the three stopped the
next — because a note in prose is read by whoever happens to open that page, while a
census is re-run by everyone. **D171 pinned the sentence as a STRING in
`expShare.test.ts`**, beside `programFor("sv02-148") === undefined` and
`FIXTURE_POOL["sv02-148"] === undefined`, so a fourth census cannot rediscover it as
news and authoring it can never be silent. **The general rule: when a census's own
pattern provably cannot see a row you know about, the fix is an ASSERTION, not a
paragraph** — this is the same move D164's Exp. Share absence-pin made, read from the
other direction.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D173) — A DECLARATION IS NOT A FIX. WHEN BOTH ARE ONE LINE,
FIX IT.** Six fixtures carried a printed attack at the wrong index. All six were
**declared**, correctly and legibly, with stated reasons: two section comments in
`testFixtures.ts` said in as many words *"a fixture's `index: 0` is Slither Wing's and
Koraidon's SECOND printed attack"*, and `catalogManifest.test.ts` held six `reindexed:
true` rows. **The declaration is what let them live.** It made a wrong index legible
**without making it wrong**, and a suite pinning `index: 0` stayed green because the
FIXTURE had been bent to fit the pin. **A declaration converts a defect into a documented
condition, and a documented condition has no pressure on it.** The economics are the whole
warning: **the entry cost about one line and the fix cost about one attack row, so the
entry won every time it was offered — four slices running.** The same trap re-armed itself
inside D173 itself: its own `types` sweep first enumerated all five divergences as
declared exceptions, and Klefki's was **fixed at the merge instead** on exactly this
ground. **So: when you are about to add an enumerated exception, price the FIX in the same
breath. If they are within a line of each other, the exception is not a mitigation — it is
the reason nobody will ever do the work.** (The declaration table is still right to
exist, and D173's is kept and pinned EMPTY: the table's job is to make an omission
NAMEABLE, not to make it permanent.)

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D173) — A FIXTURE'S BLAST RADIUS CROSSES THE PACKAGE
BOUNDARY.** Nineteen `{ type: "attack", index }` declarations named a fixture's number
instead of the card's. An engine-scoped grep found **sixteen**. The other **three** live
in **`src/features/game/GameHud.cardplay.dom.test.tsx`** — outside `packages/` entirely —
and were found **only by the suite going RED** on the first `bun run check` after the
first card was corrected. `FIXTURE_POOL` is imported by the web HUD's DOM tests to build
real boards, so **any sweep for *"who names an index for this card"* that stops at
`packages/engine/src` is short by construction.** The slice brief already said *"there may
be more; grep per card rather than trusting the list"* and that was **still not enough** —
**the missing axis was the DIRECTORY, not the card.** Grep the whole repo for a fixture
id, not the package that defines it.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D173) — A TRUNCATED FIXTURE SILENTLY SHRINKS EVERY CENSUS
THAT SWEEPS THE POOL.** `selfCounterMultiply`, `selfScalingPenalty` and
`opponentCounterScaling` each discover their producers **from the population rather than
from a list** — the design D167 and D168 were deliberately built on — and **all three had
been sweeping Arcanine ex `sv01-032`, a body that PRINTS their family's sentence, and
seeing NOTHING**, because the fixture carried only its second attack. `clauseApostrophe`'s
derivable-sentence census was short by one for the same reason (64, not 65). **Nothing in
any of those results said so**: a census over a truncated population returns a smaller
number and looks exactly like a correct census over a smaller family. *"Discovered from
the population, not enumerated"* is the right design **and it is not self-validating —
its INPUTS were short, not its PREDICATE.** This is D156's scope rule pointed at the
**FIXTURE POOL** instead of at the catalog: **a pool census owes its population the same
scrutiny a catalog census owes its row count**, and any completeness fix to a fixture owes
every pool census a re-run.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D175) — A DIVERGENCE'S *SHAPE* TELLS YOU ITS CAUSE, AND ITS
*VALUE* DOES NOT. CLASSIFY BY CONSTRUCTION SITE.** D173's `types` sweep found five
divergences and split them into *two a human WROTE* and *three the `battler` helper's
`["Colorless"]` DEFAULT showing through*, handing the second group forward as wanting **a
rule, not three edits**. The rule was built (`battler` derives an unnamed `types` from
`CATALOG_MANIFEST.printed`) and **it fixed TWO of the three.** **Arboliva `sv01-023` is not
a `battler` call at all** — a raw object literal (a Stage 1 with an `evolveFrom`, so it
never went through the helper) whose `["Colorless"]` was **WRITTEN**, copied from the
helper's shape rather than from the card. It took a hand-edit to `["Grass"]`, and **only
the sweep going red said so.** *"Fixture Colorless, print Grass"* is **the same
OBSERVATION** for a defaulted value and a hand-written one; **the two are distinguishable
only at the CONSTRUCTION SITE, and D173 inferred the cause from the VALUE.** The written
column was **3 of 5, not 2** — and it was the whole population. **A DEFECT FILED UNDER THE
WRONG CLASS IS ONE A RULE AIMED AT THAT CLASS WILL MISS.** So: **before you write a rule
for a class, grep how many members of the class actually go through the helper** — `blank`
(the raw-literal base) and `battler` are two different construction sites, and only one is
reachable by a change to `battler`. ⚠️ **The companion case is Spiritomb `sv02-089`, and it
is the same lesson from the other side: its fixture said `types: ["Darkness"]` where the
card prints `["Psychic"]` and its `weaknesses_json` is `[{"type":"Darkness","value":"×2"}]`
— the WEAKNESS value written into the type field, one column over. A WRONG COLUMN LOOKS
EXACTLY LIKE A WRONG ELEMENT**, and it reads as *deliberate* rather than as a typo
precisely because the value is real, plausible and agrees with the card on the adjacent
line. This is D173's own *"the missing axis was the DIRECTORY, not the card"* one level in:
**the missing axis is HOW THE FIXTURE WAS BUILT, not what it holds.**

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D175) — AN ALLOWLIST WITH ENTRIES HAS NO EMPTINESS LEVER, SO AN
OMISSION CAN ALWAYS HIDE IN IT.** D173's remedy for a declaration table that nobody would
ever empty was to empty it and then **pin the emptiness** (`expect(shifted).toEqual([])`),
which converts the next defect from a table entry into a FAILURE. D175 did the same for
`TYPES_DIVERGE` (`expect(diverged).toEqual([])`) — **and that move is only available to a
table that actually empties.** `catalogManifest.test.ts`'s **`INCOMPLETE` legitimately holds
~30 entries** for bodies that only ever defend, so there is no `[]` to pin it to, and the
mutation pass proves the consequence: **DROP Spiritomb's "Fade Out" and RE-DECLARE it in
`INCOMPLETE` is GREEN.** That is exactly the move D173 named as the defect, still available
on the ATTACK axis, and **it cannot be closed the way the type axis was.** The honest
statement, carried as a named remainder below rather than patched: **`INCOMPLETE` remains a
table an omission can hide in.** The general rule: **the type axis got a pin because it
EARNED one by emptying; a table that cannot empty has no equivalent, so "a declaration is
not a fix" is STRUCTURAL there rather than a matter of discipline** — and the next slice
that empties a whole cast out of such a table should ask whether the cast can be **PINNED**
rather than merely shrunk.

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D174) — A CENSUS IS ONLY AS WIDE AS ITS VERBS. ENUMERATE THE
PREDICATES, NOT ONLY THE COLUMNS.** D172's three-column rule (above, the fifteenth dangerous
claim) is **necessary and not sufficient**, and D174 is the proof. Every sweep of the §12
status-immunity family since D159 matched the IMMUNITY vocabulary — *"can't be {Burned |
Paralyzed | …}"*, *"affected by … Special Condition"* — over **all three text columns**, and it
got the immunity family **exactly right**: 4 printings / 3 sentences, re-derived and EXACT.
**Then the same query was widened by ONE verb the card it was pricing also prints —
`%recovers from%` — and FOUR MORE PRINTINGS FELL OUT that nobody had ever counted**: Gardevoir ex
`sv01-086`/`-228`/`-245` "Miracle Force" and Blissey `sv01-145` "Busybody Nurse", both *"recovers
from ALL Special Conditions"*, both DISCRETE, both unbuilt. **THE COLUMN COVERAGE WAS RIGHT AND
THE PREDICATE WAS SHORT.** A sentence with two clauses has two verbs, and **nothing in a sweep
for the first can ever see the second** — the miss is invisible to every check a column-coverage
rule performs, because the query was complete on the axis it was audited on. The concrete
instruction: **before you trust a family census, write down the VERBS a printing in that family
could use, and sweep each of them.** A card already in the census is the cheapest possible source
of the ones you forgot — *read the printing you are building, and sweep its other clause.*

⚠️ **NEW STANDING WARNING (D174) — A REASON EXPIRES WITH THE FACT IT RESTED ON. A DEFERRED
DECISION MUST RECORD WHAT WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE FOR IT TO BE REVISITED.** D172 kept
`PassiveEffects.statusImmunity` a SCALAR, and it applied this repo's own rule correctly on the
evidence it had (*the unit of STORAGE is decided by the WRITE sites; COUNT THE WRITERS* — two,
each naming one condition). It even **named the counter-case** — Therapeutic Energy names three —
and declined the widening **on one stated ground: the third writer *"cannot reach the field"***,
an Energy being neither a top card nor a Tool. **That was TRUE when it was written. Two slices
later `EnergyProgram.passive` made it FALSE, and the moment it did, the refusal had no argument
left** — the scalar could no longer SPELL a writer, and it widened. **A refusal recorded with its
REASON is worth more than a refusal recorded as a verdict** (this page's oldest standing note),
and D174 sharpens it: **write down the OBSERVATION the refusal depends on, so a later slice can
see when it stops holding.** *"Declined: no writer can reach this field"* is a claim about the
code, and the slice that adds the reach is the slice that owes the re-read — it will only know
that if the dependency was written down. ⚠️ **The same shape, one level up: D172 declined a
Checkup gate on TWO reasons, and D174 found that reason (b) had become false while reason (a)
held. The conclusion survived. It survived by luck of the second reason, not by the first one
being checked.**

**⚠️ THE CATALOG IS WHOLE AND THE HONESTY TABLE IS EMPTY. The census-scope caveat
that dominated four handoffs is now HISTORY, and it should stop being restated as a
live hazard.**

The local D1 lost the whole `swsh10.5` set (88 rows) to an uncheckpointed WAL
between 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-03; **D160 re-ingested it and checkpointed it.** Six
decisions censused the shrunken catalog (D154–D159), and
`catalogManifest.CATALOG_MANIFEST.history.censusedInTheGap` is that list in code.
**Every one of those censuses has now been re-run. D160 reversed three downward
corrections, D161 re-ran §D147's and it did not move (its date was 2026-08-02, so it
was never a floor), and D162 re-ran the last four — all UNCHANGED, with `swsh10.5`
contributing ZERO rows to any of them.** The table D160 opened is closed:

| whose | the query | claimed | re-run against 978 / 6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| D157 | `LIKE '%can''t use that attack%'` | 2 rows | **2 — D162** |
| D158 | `LIKE '%damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon%'` | 8 rows | **8 — D162** |
| D158 | `LIKE '%Knocked Out by damage from an attack%'` | 6 rows | **6 — D162** |
| D159 | `LIKE '%by attacks from%'` outside `attacks_json` | 6 rows | **6 — D162** |
| D154 | `LIKE '%During your next turn, this Pokémon can''t use %'` | 6 / 4 names | **8 / 6 names — D160, landed at D162** |
| D149/D151 | `LIKE '%less damage (before applying%'` | 5 rows | **6 — D160; both original counts EXACT** |
| D155 | `LIKE '%more damage (before applying%'` | 1 row | **1 — D160** |
| §D147 | `LIKE '%less damage%'`, all 3 columns | 31 / 14 | **31 / 14 — D161, UNCHANGED (dated 2026-08-02)** |

**⚠️ THE LESSON, IN THREE PARTS NOW.** **(1) A count a query cannot reproduce is not
thereby WRONG — the query owes its SCOPE** (D154/D155 corrected downward and were
wrong; D156 refused and was right; all three corrections are reversed by
measurement). **(2) A SCOPE TAG owes the DATE of the query it labels** (D161
corrected two 2026-08-02 censuses that D156 had mechanically tagged with today's
population). **(3) — new at D163 — A CENSUS HAS TWO NUMBERS AND THEY GO STALE
SEPARATELY.** Nine slices carried *"5 printings / 3 sentences"* for the self-scaling
group. The printing count was exact; **the sentence count was never right**, and no
amount of re-running the printing query would have found it, because it is a claim
about the DISTINCT STRINGS rather than about the rows. **Re-derive both.**

**⚠️ THE CATALOG FACTS, FOR ANY NEW CENSUS.**

🛑 **READ THIS BEFORE PLANNING ANY CENSUS — D183, session #161. THE LOCAL D1 IS NOT
IN THE REPO AND CANNOT BE RECREATED ON A FRESH MACHINE.** `.wrangler/` is gitignored,
so a fresh clone has **no sqlite at all** (`find / -name '*.sqlite'` → zero rows), and
the re-ingest path is not available either: on the Claude-Code-on-the-web runner
`api.tcgdex.net` is **refused by the network policy** (the agent proxy answers
`403` to `CONNECT`), `api.cloudflare.com` likewise, and there are no Wrangler
credentials for the remote D1. **Every census in `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md`
and every "re-derive the numbers, it's quick" instruction on this page assumes a
database that only exists on the machine that ingested it.** Consequences, in order
of how much they cost:
- **A card slice whose printed sentence is not already recorded IN THE REPO cannot be
  built safely.** `deriveAttackEffect`'s regexes are `^…$`-anchored with a required
  trailing period, so a regex written from a *paraphrase* passes a test written
  against the same paraphrase and **matches no real card** — a silently dead arm,
  which is strictly worse than an unbuilt one. The surviving in-repo sources of
  verbatim printed text are, in order of authority: `testFixtures.ts` fixtures →
  verbatim strings pinned in `*.test.ts` → the census tables in
  `reference/coverage-backlog.md` (PROSE, and exactly the class of claim this page's
  own warnings say rots).
- **`catalogManifest.ts` is NOT a substitute.** It records `name`, `types`, attack
  NAMES and ability NAMES for its 222 rows — **no effect text of any kind**.
- **The generator cannot run**, so any manifest change (e.g. recording a carried
  attack's `cost`/`damage`/`effect`) is blocked, not merely deferred.
- **To restore it**, one of: allow `api.tcgdex.net` through the environment's network
  policy and run `apps/api/scripts/ingest.ts`; or start the session with
  `tcgdex/cards-database` as an initial source (`add_repo` refuses to add it
  mid-session — cross-owner adds are unsupported); or run on a machine that has the
  `.wrangler/` state.

The local D1 holds **978 rows / 6 sets** (`sv01` 258, `sv02` 279, `sv03` 230,
`sv06.5` 99, `sve` 24, `swsh10.5` 88), `sets` **6**, `series` **2**, 708,608 bytes.

**⚠️ ITEMS 0a AND 0b ARE THE TWO UNFIXED `/code-review` FINDINGS (D153), CARRIED
FORWARD UNCHANGED.** Neither is a bug today; both are traps armed for a specific

- **0a + 5 — ONE SLICE, NOT TWO (D161 established this and D163 re-confirms it is
  untouched). `interpreter.ts`'s `attackEffectRefused` gate on `discardEnergy` tests
  the victim's ACTIVE block but refuses the WHOLE op**, and `placeSnipe`'s
  put-counter arm has **no `attackEffectRefused` check at all** where the Active arm
  (`damageActive`) has one. They are the same slice because `attackEffectRefused`
  takes a SEAT and reads that seat's **ACTIVE**, while `placeSnipe`'s arm targets a
  **BENCHED** body — so adding the call before narrowing the refusal would refuse a
  bench counter on the strength of the Active's block, i.e. 0a's defect widened.
  **Narrow the refusal to the blocked TARGET first, then the bench arm can consult
  it.** Latent today: the board-wide discard arms exist only inside `trainer:`
  programs, which never carry `invokedBy: "attack"`, and a wide block can only ever
  be live on an Active. It is a **trap for the first attack printing of a board-wide
  discard**, and that slice will not think to look here. ⚠️ **The line number in
  D153's note (`:1007`) has MOVED FIVE TIMES — grep for the gate, do not trust it.**
  ⚠️ **D157 is the third op to copy that placement** (correct for a whole-op refusal
  because its op has exactly one target); if this is taken, check the narrowing does
  not disturb it — **and D159's three read sites in the same file (`spreadDamage`,
  `placeSnipe`, `snipeActive`) are PREVENTIONS rather than refusals and must not be
  folded in with them; D161 added a term to each of the same three.**
  ⚠️ **SEVEN HANDOFFS OLD** (D150 → D154 → D155 → D156 → D157 → D160 → D161 → D163).
- **0b. `attack.ts` — `takeFlips` is the engine's ONLY `throw`, and it sits on the

**⚠️ THE FIVE STRUCTURAL QUESTIONS EVERY ENGINE SLICE OWES.** (1) Does the op you
touched **PARK** — or merely get **PERSISTED**? **A required field on
`InPlayPokemon` is a `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` bump** (D124's trigger, hit EIGHT times:
D124/D142/D143/D147/D149/D152/D154/D155, and D154→D155 is the first CONSECUTIVE
pair). An OPTIONAL field, a new union member, a new EVENT and a new enum value are
all WIDENINGS — D144 is the worked example on the sharp edge, D146 the third distinct
no-bump reason (an OPTIONAL field INSIDE a persisted SUB-RECORD), D148 the fourth (no
persisted STATE key moved), D153 the fifth (an EVENT field — `GameEvent` is persisted
NOWHERE), D156 the sixth (a TEST-ONLY module), **D157 the seventh — a new PROMPT KIND
and a new OP MEMBER, both of which DO cross into `MatchRecord` on a parked phase and
are both union WIDENINGS** — and **D159/D161 the eighth: a new
`PassiveEffects`/`StadiumEffects` field is CATALOG data read through a pure function
of the current state. D162, D163, D167, D168 and D170 are the ninth kind and the
cheapest: a
slice that adds NO persisted shape at all** (D162 a fixture and a deck; D163 a regex, a
reader and two lines of arithmetic; **D167 a regex and an `if`** — the cheapest instance
of the cheapest kind; **D168 and D170 a regex, a reader arm, a union member and an
evaluator arm each**). ⚠️ **D168 is also the sharpest statement of the rule, because it
DID add a union
member and still bought no bump: `DamageCountSource` is a PARSE-TIME type in
`effects.ts` that NEVER REACHES `GameState`, so no stored record can contain it and no
new member can make one unreadable — which is precisely the contrast with D165, whose
CHANGED `InPlayPokemon` field did.** ⚠️ **AND D170 RE-DERIVED THAT ANSWER RATHER THAN
INHERITING IT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF A CONTROL**: the shape of its change is identical
to D168's, but it was also checked against its OWN novelty — **reading a new ZONE reads
an EXISTING field off EXISTING bodies and stamps nothing** — and the no-bump is pinned
as an ABSENCE over the 16-key `InPlayPokemon` set **on a BENCHED body as well as an
Active**, the first time that pin has been taken off the bench. ⚠️ **AND D169 IS THE TWELFTH CONTROL FOR A
DIFFERENT REASON AGAIN — A FIELD ON A WIRE PROJECTION.**
`RedactedAttack.effectiveCost?: string[]` is a new `@luminous/schema` field, which looks
like the sharpest bump trigger yet and is not one: **`RedactedAttack` is rebuilt from
`GameState` on every frame and persisted nowhere**, so no stored record can contain it,
and `MatchRecord` persists exactly `{version, seed, startedAt, names, state, log}`.
Nothing was stamped onto `InPlayPokemon` — both of D169's prints are live-read ABILITIES,
which is precisely why both are §9-suppressible where a stamp would not be.
⚠️ **AND D171 IS THE FOURTEENTH CONTROL, AND THE FIRST ONE WHOSE ANSWER HAD TO SURVIVE A
FALSE PREMISE.** Its recon reasoned *"a `PendingStage` kind is transient, so it is not
persisted"* — **factually wrong: `GameState.pending` IS persisted**, and a park
mid-attack is a live, reachable, stored position. ⚠️ **RECORD THAT, because two
consecutive handoffs assumed otherwise.** The answer is still 11, but it comes from
D124's test being **DIRECTIONAL**: *can the PREVIOUS deploy's RECORD hold the shape the
NEW code expects?* An old record **cannot contain a `koToolTrigger`** (nothing wrote
one) and every kind it CAN contain is still handled; the `moveEnergy` `route` change is
a **WIDENED ENUM** on an op that *can* sit in `phase.cont`, which D124 explicitly
excludes; **no REQUIRED field was added to anything persisted**; and `ENERGY_MOVED.fromUid`
rides `GameEvent`, which `MatchRecord` does not store (it stores the RENDERED log).
⚠️ **The sharp contrast: a new ADDITIVE `PendingStage` KIND passes this test; a new
REQUIRED FIELD on an EXISTING kind would NOT.** *"Is this type persisted at all?"* is the first
question, before "is this member a widening?".
⚠️ **AND D172 IS THE FIFTEENTH CONTROL, AND THE CHEAPEST KIND OF ALL — NOTHING IT ADDS
REACHES `GameState` AT ALL.** `PassiveEffects.statusImmunity` is a **CATALOG** field
(registry.ts types); `passivesOf().statusImmunities` is a pure function of the live board
and is **never stamped**; and `STATUS_PREVENTED` rides `GameEvent`, which `MatchRecord`
does not store (it stores the RENDERED log). No key moved on `InPlayPokemon`, no
`PendingStage` kind was added, no required field landed on anything persisted — and **the
dodge was PRICED AND REFUSED (D155)**: a cached "cannot be Burned" flag on
`InPlayPokemon` would go stale on an evolution, a promotion or a lock arriving, and would
have bought a bump for nothing. **A continuous read of catalog data is the answer to this
question, not a state field — for the third `PassiveEffects` slice running.**
D148, D151, D153, D156, D157, D159, D161,
D162, D163, D166, D167, **D168 — the ELEVENTH control**, **D169, the TWELFTH**,
**D170, the THIRTEENTH**, **D171, the FOURTEENTH**, **D172, the FIFTEENTH**, **D173, the
SIXTEENTH**, **D175, the SEVENTEENTH, whose derivation is the sharpest one-liner the
question has produced: a `MatchRecord` stores card IDs, never `Card` bodies, so a fixture's
`types` and attack list are not in the record at all** — and ⚠️ **D174, the EIGHTEENTH, and the
first control whose slice WRITES TO A PERSISTED OBJECT and still owes nothing**: `recoverStatuses`
mutates `InPlayPokemon.conditions`, but it **writes an EXISTING field** (`rotation` /
`poisonDamage` / `burned` before and after, **asserted on the in-play object's own key set**), no
key moved, and the one widened shape — `STATUS_CLEARED.reason` gaining a sixth value — rides
`GameEvent`, which `MatchRecord` does not store. **"Nothing reaches `GameState`" and "the write
lands in a field that was already there" are two different clean answers to this question, and
D174 is the first to give the second** —
sitting between the bumping
slices are the CONTROLS that show the trigger is
literally "a required key appeared on `InPlayPokemon`". The test is never "did a field
land in a persisted shape" but **"can the previous deploy's RECORD hold the new
TYPE"**. **D155 adds the other half: PRICE THE DODGES AND SAY WHY YOU REFUSED THEM.
D157 adds: IF YOUR OP PARKS, SAY EXPLICITLY WHAT ITS CONTINUATION AND ITS PROMPT DO
TO THE PERSISTED SHAPE. D161 adds: PIN THE NO-BUMP AS AN ABSENCE — assert
`InPlayPokemon`'s whole key set, so a later slice adding a key goes red there.**
(2) **Whose VOICE does every row render in?** `seat` on `COUNTERS_PLACED`/`HEALED`/
`STATUS_*`/`ATTACK_BLOCK_APPLIED`/`ATTACK_LOCKED`/`DAMAGE_REDUCTION_APPLIED`/
`ATTACK_DEBUFF_APPLIED`/`RECOIL_ARMED`/`ATTACK_BOOSTED` owns the AFFECTED Pokémon,
not the actor (D136's finding 1). D153 left the general rule: *causer === seat →
ACTIVE; causer always the other seat → VICTIM-side; causer is the RULES → SYSTEM;
**and when one event type has paths where that relation DIFFERS, the relation is a
FIELD the event must carry.*** **D154 adds: the relation can be constant while what
is TRUE varies. D155 adds: whether that narrowing field is OPTIONAL is decided by the
OP, not by the path. D157 adds: WHEN TWO EARLIER SLICES EACH MOVED ONE AXIS OF A ROW,
THE CELL WHERE BOTH MOVE IS UNVERIFIED. D159 adds the sharpest: ASK WHETHER THE ROW
YOU NEED ALREADY EXISTS AND IS SIMPLY UNRENDERED — `DAMAGE_DEALT.prevented` had been
emitted since 0.58.0 with nothing reading it. D161 ran that check and the answer was
YES, IT IS READ, which is what makes it cheap: one grep of `log.ts` for the field you
are about to feed. D162 adds the inverse case: a branch that is TRUE EITHER WAY on
your printing is still worth keeping, and is worth PINNING precisely because its
mutation is otherwise invisible. And D163 adds the one that cost it a design: A FIELD
CAN BE DIRECTION-COMMITTED WITHOUT SAYING SO IN ITS TYPE — read its PRESENCE GUARD
and its RENDERER before you put a new sign in it.** **A field whose absence is
unreachable is not optional. RENDER THE ROW UNDER THE SEAT YOU RENDER IT UNDER, AND
READ IT.** (3) Is the guard you rely on ASSERTED anywhere, or an accident of a flag
chosen for another reason? **SWEEP rather than list, and ask what your sweep does NOT
traverse.** **D154 adds: MUTATE THE THING YOU JUST WROTE — and the fix for a free
guard is a WITNESS (a card), not a note.** **D156 adds the inverse for data: a sweep
over a POPULATION owes that population's size and shape.** **D157 adds the
counter-case to D154's rule: a guard that survives mutation is not automatically free
— ask whether the mutation measured THAT guard or a stricter one beside it, and keep
it (with the reason written down) when the answer is the second. D161 adds the payout
that makes free reads worth their line: `spreadDamage` and `placeSnipe`'s bench arm
carried a reduction term UNREACHABLY from 0.96.0 to 0.107.0 and a seat-wide printing
four slices later made both live with no diff. D163 adds the third disposition for a
surviving guard: KEEP IT AS THE FILE'S OWN IDIOM (three sibling calls should read the
same way) and turn the unreachability into a POOL-WIDE ASSERTION rather than a
comment — and SWEEP IN BOTH DIRECTIONS when your claim is about a PAIR, so a reader
that started answering both would collapse the two lists.**
⚠️ **D172 ADDS THE FOURTH DISPOSITION, AND IT IS THE ONE THE PRECEDENTS DID NOT COVER:
ASK WHETHER YOUR SURVIVOR IS A *GUARD* OR AN *ORDERING*.** Its M8 — placing the new
`applyStatus` immunity gate AHEAD of `attackEffectRefused` instead of behind it —
survived, and **D154's delete-the-free-guard precedent does not reach it at all, because
there is nothing to delete**: the gate is REQUIRED in both positions and only its POSITION
is free. Both orderings produce the identical board on every reachable input; only the log
row would differ, and the two gates can never both be live (a §11 block installs only on
the attacker's own Active, an attack ends the turn, and neither immune printing has such
an attack). So the D159/D161/D163 standard applies — **keep it, and turn the
unreachability into an ASSERTION** over the fixtures' printed attack text and over
`attackBlock` being null. **"Delete or witness" is a question about GUARDS; for an
ORDERING the only answers are "assert why it cannot matter" or "find the board where it
does".** ⚠️ **AND D174 IS THE SECOND SLICE RUNNING WHOSE ONLY SURVIVOR IS AN ORDERING**, which
promotes this from a precedent to a pattern: its M8 moves `recoverStatuses` ahead of Jet's
on-attach switch, the call is **required in both positions and only its POSITION is free**, and
it was kept with three assertions in place of a comment (the only `onAttach` arm fires on a BENCH
attach; `switchInto` clears the outgoing Active itself; **no card in the pool prints both an
on-attach clause and a continuous recovery**). ⚠️ **Its other mutation finding is D171's rule
paying out a second time: M4 — reading `statusImmunities` inside the recovery — is
BEHAVIOUR-IDENTICAL on the card that motivated the slice**, because *"those Special Conditions"*
makes the two lists equal, **so the witness had to come from a card printing only ONE clause.**
*A mutant that copies a sibling's real code needs a board the sibling never has.* (4) Does the mechanism
you are pricing actually exist — read the code (D135, D141, D143, D146, D147, D148,
D149). **D155 adds the inverse: check whether the ARGUMENT for your design is
DRIVEABLE, not only true. D156 adds: check whether your PREDECESSOR'S FINDING is
driveable. D161 adds: a predecessor's PRICING OF A SHAPE is not a finding at all, it
is a guess that was never compiled. D163 adds: WHEN A PREDECESSOR PRICES YOUR SLICE
AS "X ALREADY EXISTS, JUST ADD Y", THE THING TO OPEN IS NOT X BUT X's CONSUMERS.**
(5) If your slice gates an ACTION rather than an op, it owes BOTH payability
projections — `redactedAttacksOf`/`redactedRetreatOf` (redact.ts) **and**
`GameHud.tsx` — **and D157 adds: verify which SEAT the projection is computed for.**
**D163 adds the negative form, which is easy to skip: if your slice does NOT gate an
action, SAY SO WITH A BOARD — the sharp case is the one where a player would expect a
refusal and must not get one** (a self-scaling attack reduced to 0 damage is still
legal to declare). Also: if you add an op you owe the §11 classification table
(`preventBlock.test.ts`) **a verdict AND a driven board** (D150); if you add a
real-card FIXTURE you owe `catalogManifest.test.ts` either a clean diff or a declared
omission WITH A REASON (D156); and **if you add an `EffectPrompt` KIND you owe FOUR
arms in one slice — `@luminous/schema`'s `redactedEffectPromptSchema`, `redactPrompt`
(redact.ts), `effectDecisionFromPrompt` (projection.ts) and a dialog in
`GameHud.tsx` — because `apps/api/src/lobby/match.ts` puts `resolveEffect` on the
DO's allowlist EXACTLY WHILE every kind has one, and only three of the four are
compiler-enforced (D157).**

**⚠️ THE OTHER STANDING NOTES, UNCHANGED AND STILL TRUE.**
- **A CENSUS RUN FOR ONE PURPOSE IS A FLOOR FOR EVERY OTHER PURPOSE** (D142's rule,
  fifteen payouts). Before trusting a closed census for a NEW question, read its
  **QUERY**, not its conclusion — **its SCOPE (D154)**, **the numbers it quotes for
  provenance rather than for use (D155)**, **the DATE, which since D161 decides
  whether a re-run should be expected to move at all**, and — since D163 — **WHICH
  of its numbers has ever actually been re-derived** (a "N printings / M sentences"
  census has two, and only the first is what the query returns).

  D156 a TEST says so instead of a comment. `catalogManifest.test.ts`. ⚠️ **D163 adds
  the inverse and it is a gift rather than a hazard: a fixture can be RIGHT by
  COMPLETENESS and carry a printing nothing reads. Sweep the pool for your sentence
  BEFORE you write a fixture.** ⚠️ **AND D173/D175 ADD THE THIRD FORM, WHICH IS THE ONE
  THAT SURVIVES A TEST: a fixture can be wrong by VALUE, and it survives exactly as long

**Below this line: the CARRIED-FORWARD lessons of D141–D151, kept because they still
stand. They are context, not work, and their "item N" cross-references point at the
NUMBERING OF THEIR OWN LISTS — read them for the reasoning, not for the queue.**

**Carried forward from D151 (context, not work):**
- **THE HONESTY MARKER WORKED.** D150 marked its list as unverified; D151 re-queried and
  could report, precisely, which claims held. Keep marking. It costs a sentence and it is
  the only thing that makes "verify before you cost" actionable rather than pious.
- **AN AURA IS NOT A FOLD.** `passivesOf` reads the HOLDER. Any printed sentence whose
  subject is the holder's OPPONENT needs a scan of its own, and `opposingAttackDebuff` is
  now the seventh worked example. Check WHOSE card the sentence is about before choosing a
  shape — items 3 and 4 below are both this question.
- **ONE BOARD CAN PROVE AN ASYMMETRY THAT TWO BOARDS ONLY ILLUSTRATE.** The §9 pair
  (aura silenced, stamp paying) is one state with one field flipped, plus a control that
  stops the positive case passing for the wrong reason. Prefer that to two similar boards.
- **THE SAME CLAUSE CAN ANSWER DIFFERENTLY AT TWO SITES AND STILL BE ONE READING.**
  `ignoreWR` nulls the aura at `snipeActive` (source and target coincide) and not at
  `placeSnipe` (they do not). Resolve such a question by asking WHICH BODY the printed
  clause names, not by making the code uniform.

**Carried forward from D150 (context, not work) — and this run's LAST lesson:**
- **A TEST THAT FORCES A QUESTION IS NOT A TEST THAT CHECKS THE ANSWER, AND WRITING THAT
  DOWN THREE TIMES IS NOT FIXING IT.** D148 measured it, D149 re-measured it, D150
  measured it a third time and then paid the ~1 hour it cost. **If a finding survives two
  handoffs unfixed, fix it on the third rather than re-reporting it.**
- **A PROOF MUST BE TWO-SIDED.** Driving only the `blocked` half would have passed a guard
  that refused EVERYTHING. Whenever a classification has two values, drive both.
- **SHARPENING A VOCABULARY IS A WAY OF FINDING BUGS.** Restating `blocked`/`untouched`
  as "what a live block DOES" rather than "who owes the check" moved `damageDefender` on
  the spot. Ask what a label MEANS on a board before trusting the label.
- **A SWEEP'S BLINDNESS RECURS ONE LEVEL OUT.** D148 fixed the WALKER (nested op bodies);
  D150 found the SOURCE sweep missing a whole reader (`deriveAttackCoinFlip`'s
  `programPerHeads.ops`). Ask not only "what does my walker descend" but **"how many
  functions hand an attack a PROGRAM"** — the answer is two, not one.
- **AN UNREACHABLE ASYMMETRY IS STILL WORTH WRITING DOWN WITH ITS LINE NUMBER** (item 7).

**Carried forward from D149 (context, not work):**
- **A FIXTURE CAN BE WRONG BY OMISSION.** Florges `sv01-093` sat in `FIXTURE_POOL` from
  D104 to D149 with no `attacks` array, on a card with exactly one printed attack. Every
  assertion about it passed; the producer sweep could not see it. Diff a fixture against
  its D1 row FIELD BY FIELD, including the fields it does not have.
- **A FUNCTION'S NAME IS NOT ITS CONTRACT.** `attackerPreWRBonus` reads like "a number"
  and is a `passivesOf` fold — §9-suppressible, and REPORTED as a positive on
  `DAMAGE_DEALT.bonus`. Both facts decided the slice's shape. Read what a function FOLDS
  before extending it, not just what it returns.
- **A DESIGN QUESTION IS CHEAP TO ANSWER ONLY IF THE ANSWER IS GROUNDED IN SOMETHING A
  TEST CAN SEE.** "A reported field would drop the number", "a catalog fold is
  §9-suppressible and an installation must not be", "only this term can go negative" are
  all checkable. Write those, not the preference.
- **A TEMPLATE QUOTED FROM A NEIGHBOURING CENSUS IS A COUNT COPIED FORWARD WEARING A
  REGEX.** §D147's row for this family flattened two printed sentences into one string;
  the list inherited it; it matched 2 of 5 printings. Re-query the STRING, not just the
  count.
- **A LOG ROW YOU ARE COPYING MUST BE RENDERED UNDER THE SEAT YOU WILL RENDER IT UNDER.**
  D147's wording is honest under the installer's name and false under the victim's, and
  nothing but reading it says so.
- **PRINTED SCOPE IS A CENSUS ANSWER, NOT AN INTUITION.** All 12 pre-W/R printings that
  ADD damage say "to your opponent's Active Pokémon"; neither of the two that SUBTRACT
  says anything. That one query decided whether the debuff reaches the Bench.
- **A `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` CONTROL EXISTS NOW.** D147 bumped, D148 did not, D149
  bumped — three consecutive durated slices — so the trigger is demonstrably "a required
  key appeared on `InPlayPokemon`" and not "a durated effect landed".

**Carried forward from D148 (context, not work):**
- **A REFUSAL WRITTEN DOWN WITH ITS ARGUMENT IS A CHECKABLE ARTEFACT; A VERDICT IS NOT.**
  D143 declined `preventAttack` a `target` AND wrote why. D148 re-ran the argument with
  the second printing in hand and it did not hold. Neither the refusal nor the overturn
  cost anything, and both were only possible because the reasoning was in the file.
- **TWO NUMBERS ARE NOT TWO AXES IF ONE IS A FUNCTION OF THE OTHER.** The test for
  "does this field need a sibling?" is not "do the values differ" — it is "can they vary
  INDEPENDENTLY". Here they cannot: the window is always the locked Pokémon's
  controller's next turn, and §5.3 fixes the rest.
- **THE SAME PREDICATE ON A DIFFERENT BODY MAY RESOLVE AT A DIFFERENT SITE.** D146's
  `isBasicPokemon` had to be deferred to the read sites because the ATTACKER was unknown
  at install. The DEFENDER is not, so the identical predicate becomes an install-time
  `BoardCondition` and stores nothing. **Ask WHEN the body is knowable, not what the
  predicate is.**
- **A SWEEP CAN BE THE ACCIDENT.** `preventBlock.test.ts`'s walker descended
  `coinFlipGate` only for six slices, and could not fail, because the ops inside a gate
  were also emitted bare elsewhere. Ask what your sweep does not TRAVERSE, and pin the
  traversal directly when the pool cannot exercise it.
- **A TEST THAT FORCES A QUESTION IS NOT A TEST THAT CHECKS THE ANSWER.** The §11
  classification table is a forcing function — genuinely useful, and it is what found
  this slice's refusal — but a WRONG verdict goes green. Measured, not assumed (item 4).
- **A LOG ROW IS NEVER SPOKEN FROM THE INSTALLER'S CHAIR.** The printed wordings say
  "your next turn" / "your opponent's next turn" because a card addresses its user; a
  row addresses a reader looking at a board. D143 phrased `ATTACK_LOCKED` from the
  AFFECTED side and that is why D148 owed no new arm — where D146 owed a third phrasing
  because its field changed what the rule DOES.
- **"THE DEFENDING POKÉMON" IS §8 step 5's TERM OF ART**, not "whatever is Active on
  their turn": the body that was Active when the attack RESOLVED. Everything else
  follows — §10 sheds the effect on leaving or evolving, and the victim's counterplay is
  the same three routes the self-lock's holder has, with the agency inverted.
- **NOT DONE deliberately:** no `target` on `preventRetreat` (nothing prints the self
  side); no attack-address field (item 3 owns it, and it is the fifth stamped field); no
  hardening of the §11 classification table's VERDICTS (item 4 owns it — measured and
  reported rather than smuggled in); no bare defender-lock anchor (censused, printed
  nowhere standalone); no capture for the class token (D146's call, one printing); no
  `EffectContext.invokedBy` reading (the lock gates a DECLARATION, and D143's
  generalisation already settles that it needs none); no driven `effects: true` block off
  a printed card (all 13 printings of that spelling are coin-gated — censused — and the
  suite's determinism claim is that it takes no coin, so D143's surgery is reused); no
  DOM test for `GameHud.tsx` (its line is the engine predicate, called directly, and D143
  set that precedent).

**Carried forward from D147 (context, not work):**
- **THE GENERALISATION IS ANSWERED — DO NOT RE-OPEN IT ON COUNT ALONE.** A third
  parallel stamped field, and the trigger is a QUESTION SHAPE (a caller that must
  ENUMERATE the installed effects), not a number of fields. **D148 added none**, so the
  count is still three: item 2 would be the fourth and item 3 the fifth, and only the
  fifth is a trigger, because it carries a PAYLOAD (an attack index) rather than a bare
  stamp.
- **SHARING A SITE IS NOT SHARING A QUESTION.** The single most useful sentence D147
  produced. Two facts read at the same four lines still need two lookups when they are
  folded at two different STEPS of the same pipeline; a union merges storage, not reads.
- **A CENSUS SPLIT BY A PARENTHETICAL.** `takes {N} less damage … (AFTER applying
  Weakness and Resistance)` and `attacks … do {N} less damage … (BEFORE …)` are the same
  words about opposite bodies at opposite steps. **Read the parenthetical before the
  verb phrase**, and keep it INSIDE the anchor.
- **ONLY A MULTIPLICATIVE STEP MAKES AN ORDERING OBSERVABLE.** Resistance and a flat
  reduction commute, so a suite that pins "after W/R" against a Resistance-only board is
  asserting nothing. Pick fixtures for their WEAKNESS lines, and assert the reversed
  number as well as the printed one.
- **A CLAMPED ZERO IS NOT A PREVENTION.** `DAMAGE_DEALT.prevented` stays absent when a
  big reduction zeroes a hit: the §11 block SUPERSEDES the pipeline, a reduction RAN it.
  Two facts, one number.
- **THE FIXTURE POOL IS A CENSUS NOBODY RE-READS.** Two of D147's fourteen printings
  were already in it, unmapped, on cards fielded for unrelated sentences. Sweep
  `FIXTURE_POOL` for a family's sentence before costing it. (D148 ran the sweep and it
  came back EMPTY — which is the rule working, not the rule failing.)
- **A NAME CAN BE RIGHT AND WRONG IN THE SAME REPO.** `sv03-145` was "Bronzong" in
  `testFixtures.ts` and "Palafin" in five comments simultaneously. Grep the ID, not the
  name, and reconcile. (D148 re-ran that sweep and found nothing; run it anyway.)


**Carried forward from D146 (context, not work):**

  REMAINDER LIST.** "`Ancient` has no reader anywhere in the engine" was TRUE and

  row: the attack's own `DAMAGE_DEALT` is the whole story, and loudness is owed to
  UNREAD TEXT rather than to a read rule saying no (D140). But a rule that FIRES may owe
  the reader wording that says what it actually covers — hence the install row's third
  phrasing, and (D147) the AMOUNT on the reduction row.

  pin the fact by an unchanged `rngState` across a whole install (D143's move) — but

  and a species table would be WRONG); no widening of `fromClass` beyond one member; no
  `preventDamage` `target` field (no printing installs this on the defender); no fixture

**Carried forward from D144 (still current):**
- **`attack.ts` DOES NOT READ `coinFlipGate`, AND THE TWO COIN FAMILIES ARE DISJOINT BY
  WHERE THEY LAND.** `deriveAttackCoinFlip`'s union (`bonusOnHeads`, `cancelOnTails`,
  `perHeads`, `programPerHeads`) is read in FRONT of the §8.5 pipeline because those
  members retract or fold DAMAGE; `coinFlipGate` is an `EffectOp` and runs at the tail
  (D125's placement rule). **Do not repeat the resume-list error of calling
  `programPerHeads` part of the gate.** The gate's only readers are `runProgram`'s
  splice (interpreter.ts) and `programPlayable`'s descent (cardplay.ts) — **still two
  after D145, which added three producers and no reader.**
- **`coinFlipGate` CARRIES A FACE, AND IT HAS NOW BEEN SPENT.** `onTails?: true`, ABSENT
  on every heads-gated program (D135's rule, swept over the pool and the registry). D144
  predicted a future tails sentence would cost one regex; D145 wrote two and the family
  closed. The two-consequent printings still need an `otherwise`, which the op
  deliberately does not have (D142's refusal), and **the field brings them no closer** —
  say so rather than re-deriving it.
- **`programPlayable`'s DESCENT IS FACE-AGNOSTIC, AND IT IS ASSERTED.** A coin gate has
  no `otherwise`, so `then` is the only thing the card can ever do whichever face runs
  it. The pool has NO tails-gated Trainer this op can express (Egg Incubator is
  two-consequent), so the case is a constructed program — the honest shape for a rule
  with no card, and the precedent D145 reused for its unreachable empty-set whiff.
- **A SEED TABLE IS SHARED ACROSS INSTALLERS ONLY WHILE THE SURGERIES ARE RNG-PURE.**
  `setActiveFromDeck` and `attachFromDeck` consume no rng, so the install flip is the
  first coin either board draws after setup — which is why `TAILS_GATE_DECK`'s table is
  one list for two cards and `TAILS_SELF_COST_DECK`'s is one list for three. Assert it
  seed-by-seed; do not infer it. **⚠️ AND IT IS WHY A COIN SUITE GETS ITS OWN 60:** both
  tables are pinned seed by seed against their own shuffle, so adding one card to either
  deck moves all 40 of that table's pins.

**Carried forward from D143 (context, not work):**
- **"DURING YOUR NEXT TURN" IS `state.turn + 2`; "DURING YOUR OPPONENT'S NEXT TURN" IS
  `+ 1`.** Declaring an attack ENDS the turn (§5.3). Both are built and both are driven
  across real turn boundaries; **copy neither without reading which possessive the card
  prints**, because the wrong one fails QUIETLY in play rather than loudly.
- **A DURATED EFFECT DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY OWE A PROVENANCE CHANNEL.** D142 needed
  `EffectContext.invokedBy` because "effects of ATTACKS" is a claim about what INVOKED an
  effect and the target cannot answer it. D143 needed none, because every site that reads
  its field is already, by construction, about declaring an ATTACK. **Only a durated
  effect that gates an OP owes the channel.**
- **A GATE ON AN ACTION IS A REJECTION, NOT AN EVENT — AND IT OWES TWO PROJECTIONS.**
  `ATTACK_PREVENTED` joins `RETREAT_PREVENTED`; nothing is spent and the turn does not
  end (§12's Asleep shape, not §12's Confusion shape). `redactedAttacksOf`'s `banned`
  and `GameHud.tsx`'s `disabled` are the only things between a locked player and a
  rejected button. **D144's refinement: a new PRODUCER of that op owes no new line, but
  it owes evidence that it reaches the existing one.**
- **THE THREE §10 CLEAR SITES ARE HAND-WRITTEN LITERALS IN TWO FILES** —
  `clearOnLeavingActive` and `placeEvolution` (turn.ts), `switchInto` (interpreter.ts) —
  and nothing makes them agree. `attackLock.test.ts` SWEEPS them: it encumbers a
  Pokémon with every §10-sheddable field and asserts all three routes shed the same set.
  **A fourth stamped field fails there until it is added to all three.** Do not replace
  that case with a list.
- **`InPlayPokemon` CARRIES TWO TURN STAMPS AND A `promotedTurn`.** `attackBlock`
  (`+1`, D142), `attackLockedTurn` (`+2`, D143), `promotedTurn` (D124). Each is read
  through ONE `continuous.ts`-side helper, each expires by arithmetic, and none has a
  boundary clear. **D144 added none**, so a third durated field is still the
  generalisation trigger (item 4).
- **`placeSnipe`'s ACTIVE arm has a PUT-COUNTER branch** (`damageActive`, reused).
  Before D143 that branch assumed `deals` on the strength of a comment. A future
  `opponentAny` producer inherits the right behaviour for free; a future `opponentBench`
  one still cannot reach the Active at all.

**Carried forward from D142 (context, not work):**
- **A DURATED EFFECT'S LIFETIME IS A TURN STAMP, AND WHICH BOUNDARY CLEAR IS CORRECT
  DEPENDS ON WHOSE BODY IT SITS ON.** D112's §13.4 paralysis clock (clear for
  `endedSeat`) is right for a block installed on the DEFENDER and **a full turn too
  early** for one installed on the ATTACKER's own. Before reusing a lifetime, ask whose
  Pokémon carries it.
- **AN EFFECT OP CANNOT TELL AN ATTACK FROM A TRAINER, AND THE FACT BELONGS TO THE
  INVOCATION.** `EffectContext.invokedBy?: "attack"` is set by `attack.ts` alone. This
  REFINES D139 rather than reversing it: a LOG LABEL stays on the op (`damageActive`/
  `damageChosen.source`), a RULE several ops must answer identically rides the context.
  The two are pinned to AGREE on every producer in the pool.
- **"(Damage is not an effect.)" IS PRINTED IN THE POOL** — Palafin `sv03-145` "Oracle
  Press". It is the spec for every prevent/effect question, and it is why a placed damage
  COUNTER falls on the EFFECTS side (consistent with D138/D139's ruling that a placement
  is not attack damage).
- **THE §11 BLOCK'S READ SITES ARE THE SAFEGUARD SITES.** `attackBlockOf` sits beside
  `passivesOf().preventDamageFromExV` on the same `||` at `attack.ts`'s main hit,
  `spreadDamage`, `placeSnipe`'s `deals` arm and `snipeActive`. A new damage site owes
  both. The EFFECTS half is guarded at `applyStatus`, `preventRetreat`, `damageActive`,
  `moveCountersToDefender` and `discardEnergy` (opponent-side only) — and since D143
  `damageActive` also serves `damageChosen`'s Active placement, so that guard is shared.
- **A BLOCK CAN ONLY EVER BE LIVE ON AN ACTIVE**, because installing it needs an attack
  and leaving the Active Spot ends it — so the Bench-target guards are unreachable by
  construction and are written anyway. **The SELF-LOCK is the same** (D143).
- **`preventBlock.test.ts`'s CLASSIFICATION TABLE IS TOTAL OVER THE DISCOVERED OP SET**
  in both directions. A slice that teaches `deriveAttackEffect` a new op FAILS there
  until it says which side of the §11 reading that op falls on — **which is exactly what
  happened to D143's `preventAttack`, one slice later, working as designed.** Do not
  replace it with a list, and do not add an entry for an op nothing emits.


**Carried forward from D141 (still current):**
- **A LABEL ON AN AGGREGATED VALUE MUST NAME THE MECHANISM, NOT THE PROVENANCE.**

**Standing rules for any engine slice** (`docs/conventions.md` + the family's own):
`bun run check` must be green; one anchored reader per printed string, no `/i`, with
apostrophes carrying `['’]`; a NEW literal lookup table must be read through

`engineVersion` with a doc block; bump `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **only** if a

and a new enum value are all WIDENINGS (D125's distinction; D135, D137, D138, D139 and
D141 all bumped NEITHER, and D130 added a whole op without bumping either) — **but a
REQUIRED field on an op that PARKS is a persisted-shape change and DOES bump (D140), and
so is a REQUIRED field on anything `GameState` embeds, `InPlayPokemon` included (D124,
and D142 with no op change at all)**. The test is always *"can the previous deploy's
RECORD hold the old shape"*, and a field that would read back BENIGNLY is exactly what
the constant refuses. **And a LOG WORDING change never bumps**: `MatchRecord` persists the
RENDERED `SeatLogEntry[]`, so an old record holds old TEXT, which is readable by
construction (D141).

**Superseded header (build #100 — the CONDITIONAL flat attack-damage bonus, D115):**
**Last updated (was):** 2026-08-01 — build session #100 (**P3-M5 — the CONDITIONAL flat attack-damage bonus: "If \<clause\>, this attack does N more damage.", a fourth `DamageCountSource` that is a 0-or-1 INDICATOR — 11 printings / 7 cards / ZERO registry rows (D115, engine 0.66.0)**).
"If \<clause\>, this attack does N more damage." now SIMULATES — **the largest unbuilt attack-text family in the ingested pool** (32 distinct sentences / 43 printings), and the first long-tail slice whose value is a **shared skeleton with independently-priced predicates** rather than one card or one mechanism. **BOTH leads D114's resume point named were costed FIRST and both were corrected, one fatally.** (1) **Slither Wing `sv06.5-026` is DEAD** — the resume point's own caveat ("check first whether the catalog even carries a Future subtype field") resolved to **no**: `PRAGMA table_info(cards)` has no subtype/tag column and none that could hold one; the upstream tcgdex `suffix` field IS parsed (`packages/schema/src/tcgdex/card.ts`) but **dropped before the D1 insert**, and carries the rule-box suffix (`ex`/`V`) anyway, never the Ancient/Future tag. In the ingested pool "Future Pokémon" is a **1-card name list** (only Iron Moth `sv06.5-009` could satisfy it) that rots the moment sv04/sv05 ingest — **blocked on an INGEST change, not engine work.** (2) **The "Stadium in play" sub-shape is a SINGLETON, not the 5 printings the resume point recorded**: Falkner `sv02-180`/`-251` is **already built** (D40's `conditionGate`), and Paldean Clodsire ex `sv02-130`/`-244`'s sentence is on an **Ability** and reads *presence* ("if **a** Stadium is in play"), not the ownership `yourStadiumInPlay` encodes — a different seam. Only Palossand `sv02-096` was new. **The census that mattered was the one neither lead asked for: sweep the SKELETON, not the PREDICATE.** Three negative facts from the same sweep, each load-bearing: the pool holds **no** trailing "… more damage **if** …" (the conditional is always LEADING), **no** `If …, this attack does N **less** damage.` twin, and **no** sentence combining a leading `If` with a trailing "for each" — so this bucket and the three built scaling buckets are **disjoint by construction**, which is what makes an anchored `^If (.+), this attack does (\d+) more damage\.$` safe next to the exact `for each` arms. The 26-printing coin-flip family can never reach it (the flip sentence always precedes the `If`) and stays loud, correctly — a flip is new information and must be announced; a board condition is not (the D40 invariant). **Modelled as a fourth `DamageCountSource` member `{ kind: "boardCondition"; cond: BoardCondition }`, honestly DEGENERATE — a 0-or-1 INDICATOR**: `per × count` is then the printed flat bonus when the clause holds and 0 when it does not, so the family reuses the additive `AttackDamageBonus` fold **whole** — **no new fold in attack.ts, no new branch in the §8.5 pipeline, no new op, no new event or event field, no registry row, no web/API/DB/`@luminous/schema` diff.** D110's "a member, not a mechanism" rule, applied a second time. **The ONLY structural change: `scaledAttackDamage` gains the ATTACKER's seat** — it knew only `defenderSeat`, and a `BoardCondition` is relative to whose board it reads; `action.seat` was already in scope at the single call site (`snipeActive` does not use the function), so it is a one-argument change. The D110 payoff repeats: `effectSimulated`/`modifierSimulated` both flip purely because `scaling !== null`, so the printed `+` and the sentence stop being flagged **whether or not the condition holds** — correct, and asserted in both directions. **The clause table is a `Map<string, BoardCondition>`, NOT an object literal** — the key is arbitrary PRINTED text, and an object lookup on arbitrary text can hit `Object.prototype` (`"constructor"`, `"toString"`) and hand back something that is not a `BoardCondition`. **An UNMAPPED clause falls through to `null` and stays LOUD** (`ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`): silently scoring an unrecognised condition at 0 is a wrong number with no failure; the loud path is a visible gap. **Landed: 4 clauses, 11 printings / 11 card ids / 7 distinct cards, ZERO registry rows** — every card derives straight off its printed sentence. **TWO of the four cost ZERO new predicate code**: `yourStadiumInPlay` → Palossand `sv02-096` (+80) and `morePrizesThanOpponent` → Gyarados `sv02-043` (+100) are D40 members that **already existed**, making this family the vocabulary's **fourth consumer** and the first reached through printed ATTACK text rather than a registry row. Two new members: **`opponentActiveDamaged`** (Meowscarada ex `sv02-015/-231/-256/-271` +120, Gyarados ex `sv01-045/-225` +180 — 6 printings, the biggest single clause) and **`opponentActiveIsEvolution`** (Seviper `sv02-137` +50, Houndoom `sv03-133` +70, Toxicroak `sv06.5-024` +90), the latter reusing **D105's `evolveFromOf(card) !== null`** verbatim so the Evolution reading cannot drift from the `evolutionPokemon` CardFilter's. **The rules call: the printed "already" is a TIMING word, not a predicate refinement** — read at DECLARATION, before this attack's own damage lands, so an undamaged defender cannot bootstrap the bonus with the very hit it is scaling (Gyarados ex into a clean Active is **180, not 360**); the predicate cannot enforce that, the read site does, and `conditionNote` deliberately drops the "already" (a tooltip fragment is read in the present). `conditionalDamage.test.ts` (**28**) on a DEDICATED `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_DECK`: all four derivations; the anchor guards (the coin-flip rider, a lowercase `if`, a missing period, appended trailing text, and a well-formed but **UNMAPPED** real clause — Venoshock `sv01-128`/`sv03-129` "is Poisoned" — proving an unrecognised condition stays loud); both derivers' disjointness from `deriveAttackEffect` and `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`; each of the four board effects with its control; the Stadium **OWNERSHIP** case (the opponent's Beach Court in the same shared zone does NOT satisfy it); the "already" timing case; the Basic-vs-Evolution pair; the §8.5 fold order (the bonus lands BEFORE Weakness — Seviper into Palossand is `(50+50)×2 = 200`); **no `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` in EITHER the true or the false case**; `conditionHolds`/`conditionNote` for both new members incl. the null-Active edge and both seats; and a frozen-board purity check. New fixtures: faithful Palossand `sv02-096` (one of the few rows with a non-empty resistance, and it mixes an int-damage attack with a string-damage one in the same array), Gyarados `sv02-043`, Gyarados ex `sv01-045` and Seviper `sv02-137` (a **Basic**, so it fields in one surgery) + the deck. engineVersion 0.65.0 → **0.66.0**; `bun run check` **GREEN (exit 0): 157 → 158 files, 2165 → 2193 tests** (tsc + biome lint + vitest). getting it wrong would have been silent). **ZERO call-site churn:** the seat is derived exactly as the five siblings derive theirs, purely so "your opponent" resolves — which keeps `effectiveRetreatCost(state, pokemon)`'s signature and **all four** of its readers untouched (turn.ts's retreat gate, redact.ts's `redactedRetreatOf`, attack.ts's `scaledAttackDamage`, the web `GameHud.tsx`).
